units.function: CLI integration-test helpers that re-export the database package's embedded PostgreSQL harness and build deterministic uncompressed ZIP archives without a third-party ZIP writer.
units.dependencyDirection: The embedded database helper is a thin test-only re-export from @paperclipai/db. The ZIP helper depends only on Uint8Array and TextEncoder and is consumed by import/export and ZIP-codec tests; production feedback code separately contains another ZIP implementation.
units.keyDataModels: EmbeddedPostgresTestSupport/TestDatabase and an in-memory map of relative file paths to UTF-8 strings or bytes, encoded into ZIP local headers, central-directory entries, CRC-32 values and an end record.
units.lifecycle: Tests start isolated embedded PostgreSQL through the database-owned harness, or sort fixture files, encode stored ZIP entries, compute offsets/checksums and return deterministic archive bytes for importer/codec tests.
units.testAssessment: The two focused ZIP consumer suites passed 6/6 tests on 2026-08-19 and CLI no-emit TypeScript passed. The helper itself has no direct boundary/overflow/property tests; embedded PostgreSQL behavior is tested indirectly by larger suites and owned in the database package.
units.designRationale: Keep CLI integration tests close to production database behavior while avoiding native/external ZIP tooling and compression variability for small deterministic fixtures.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs reproducible portability and migration tests against its real supported database profiles, including malformed archive, path safety, size-limit and rollback cases.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the database-owned reusable test harness and deterministic fixture-builder pattern, not the exact Paperclip exports or archive code. Company OS should use one canonical ZIP implementation or well-maintained library, add zip-bomb/path/collision/ZIP64 limits and avoid a test implementation drifting from production.
units.responsibilityConflict: These helpers do not model identity or responsibility. Their relevance is evidentiary portability: fixtures must not be mistaken for production data, and import tests must prove provenance, authorization and rollback outside this utility.

2026-08-19 focused Vitest: 2 files and 6 tests passed
securityFindings: The helper accepts arbitrary root/relative paths and does not reject absolute paths, traversal, duplicate normalized names, control characters or reserved entries; importer security must not rely on fixture construction.
Lengths, offsets and entry counts are written as classic ZIP 16/32-bit fields without overflow or ZIP64 checks, which is acceptable only for bounded small fixtures.
No explicit archive-size, per-entry-size or compression-ratio policy is represented; production import must enforce all limits independently.
A second ZIP builder exists in production feedback code, creating duplicated format logic and a maintenance/divergence risk.
The embedded database helper is only a re-export, so isolation, teardown, credential handling and unsupported-platform behavior must be assessed in the owning database unit.
